Special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum on Online Safety to be held at 7pm Friday September 4th
item.description: A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th. The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th.

The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum will be Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Barisal, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum will focus on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

You can also be part of the live audience by applying for registration with a question that you would like to ask during the forum.

The application to register details can be found on our website and facebook page, fijivillage.

You will receive a confirmation if you have been selected to be part of the live audience.

Please apply early to avoid any disappointment.

The show will be broadcast live at 7pm Friday September 4th on our Facebook, YouTube and X.

item.title: Pacific Polytech opens training hotel to prepare students for tourism careers
item.description: Students pursuing careers in Fiji’s tourism industry now have a new place to gain practical experience, with the Pacific Polytech Melrose Hotel officially opened in Sigatoka. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Tourism and Civil Aviation Viliame Gavoka says the training hotel will give students the opportunity to learn in an environment with real guests, real service and real industry standards
item.content:encoded:
Students pursuing careers in Fiji’s tourism industry now have a new place to gain practical experience, with the Pacific Polytech Melrose Hotel officially opened in Sigatoka.

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Tourism and Civil Aviation Viliame Gavoka says the training hotel will give students the opportunity to learn in an environment with real guests, real service and real industry standards.

He says a training hotel is more than just bricks and mortar, describing it as a classroom where students can gain practical experience before entering the tourism industry.

Pacific Polytech established the Melrose Hotel as a registered training hotel for its students.

Gavoka says Pacific Polytech stepped into an important gap after the Technical Colleges of Fiji closed in late 2020 and early 2021, at a time when Fiji needed skilled workers.

He says the institution has grown from its first campus in Tavua in 2021 to a network of campuses from Lami to Labasa.

Gavoka says Pacific Polytech graduated 1,370 students in 2025, with that number expected to rise to 2,033 this year.

He says the institution offers 15 national qualifications and 22 provider qualifications.

Gavoka says tourism remains central to Fiji’s development, with the country recording 986,367 visitors and $2.81 billion in tourism earnings in 2025.

He says a strong tourism industry depends on having a trained workforce.

Gavoka also highlighted the Government’s recent legislative and policy changes affecting tourism, marine areas and aviation.

He says the Government’s focus also includes addressing the loss of skilled workers through training more people and strengthening the pipeline of skilled Fijians.

Gavoka says Government sets the policy and law, while institutions such as Pacific Polytech help build the skilled workforce needed to deliver them.

item.title: Australian support has been crucial to Fijian Drua's growth – Hussein
item.description: Speaking at the Fiji-Australia and Australia-Fiji Business Councils Joint Forum Gala Dinner , Hussein says Australia has been an important part of the Drua's journey from the beginning. He says the Drua plays and does business in Australia, has Australian sponsors and commercial partners, and has a large supporter base there.
item.content:encoded:
Speaking at the Fiji-Australia and Australia-Fiji Business Councils Joint Forum Gala Dinner , Hussein says Australia has been an important part of the Drua's journey from the beginning.

He says the Drua plays and does business in Australia, has Australian sponsors and commercial partners, and has a large supporter base there.

Hussein says the Drua took a major risk when it launched as Fiji's first professional sporting club during the COVID-19 pandemic, when borders were closed and there was uncertainty over the future of competitions.

He says the entire organisation had to relocate to Lennox Head in northern New South Wales for its first season because it could not operate normally from Fiji.

Hussein says early funding from the Australian Government, through its Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, supported professional pathways for Fijian men's and women's rugby players and gave the Drua the confidence to begin its Super Rugby journey in late 2021.

He says Rugby Australia also played an important role in administering the Australian Government's support and helping the Drua establish itself as a professional rugby organisation.

Hussein says five years later, the Drua has men's, women's and development teams and pays full-time salaries to 90 athletes and 35 staff.

He says the club has also become an important pathway to the Flying Fijians, with 29 of the 37 players in the national squad he referred to either currently playing for the Drua or having come through the club.

Hussein says the Drua has become what he describes as a living example of the strong relationship between Fiji and Australia.

He says Australian support, together with backing from the Fijian Government and commercial partners, has helped put the Drua on a path towards becoming financially self-sustaining while remaining competitive.

Hussein says increased Australian investment announced under the latest Fiji-Australia partnership will help strengthen the club, its players, teams and commercial operations while allowing it to develop other sources of income.

However, he says one of the challenges facing the Drua is retaining players when they receive significantly higher offers from clubs in countries such as France, England and Japan.

Hussein says the Drua cannot blame players for taking these opportunities, but the situation means the club must continue strengthening its system for identifying and developing the next generation of Fijian players.

He says the Drua's impact also extends beyond rugby, with overseas schools and teams increasingly travelling to Fiji to train and play, bringing visitors who spend money on flights, accommodation and other services.

Hussein says the Drua is only five years old and remains in its start-up phase, making strong partnerships and long-term support important as it works towards becoming financially sustainable.

item.title: Five inmates get a second chance after receiving presidential pardons
item.description: Five out of eight inmates have been given an opportunity to start a new chapter in their lives after receiving their official presidential pardons in Suva yesterday. Aisake Qiolele, Josefa Tukana, Mohammed Harun Khan, Sailosi Rokotuiwalevu and Tang Lu received their pardons at the Fiji Corrections Service National Headquarters.
item.content:encoded:
Five out of eight inmates have been given an opportunity to start a new chapter in their lives after receiving their official presidential pardons in Suva yesterday.

Aisake Qiolele, Josefa Tukana, Mohammed Harun Khan, Sailosi Rokotuiwalevu and Tang Lu received their pardons at the Fiji Corrections Service National Headquarters.

The pardons were formally presented by the Acting Commissioner of Corrections, together with the Acting Assistant Commissioner of Corrections Operations and the Southern and Central/Eastern Divisional Supervisors.

The officials reminded the recipients that their release marks a new beginning and encouraged them to carry forward the positive values, discipline and lifestyle developed during their time within the Corrections system.

They were also encouraged to remain committed to making better choices and avoid returning to the path that led to their incarceration.

The recipients were urged to maintain their faith in the Lord, remain steadfast in His word and use the opportunity to build lives marked by responsibility, purpose and positive change.

Eight inmates were granted presidential pardons.

The remaining three, Luke Dikevitukana, Mohammed Shaheen and Saula Rokobukai, will receive their pardons at Ba, Lautoka and Labasa Corrections Centres respectively.
